# Kraka Ravnsvake

*Pages PDF 40-47*

## ## **Kraka Ravnsvake**
## **Proudest Remaining Norse Dwarf Hold and Home of Their Greatest Navy**
## **Norse Dwarfhold**
Kraka Ravnsvake (Khazalid for ‘Raven’s Roost Hold’) is the southernmost Dwarfhold located in eastern Norsca, and a home base for the Norse Dwarf navy. Following the fall of Kraka Drak to Chaos in 2390 IC refugees found sanctuary in the lands controlled by Kraka Ravnsvake and it became foremost of the Norse Dwarfholds. In recent years many of these refugees have returned to Kraka Drak, hoping to clear the halls and repopulate the hold. 

## **Saddling Two Vales**
Kraka Ravnsvake is located on a ridge overlooking two drainage basins: River Dypvann ( _Dumaraz_ ) to the west and Draksfjord to the east. An underground passageway of canals ( _Ungruvalk_ ) beneath Kraka Ravnsvake was completed in 2292 IC, connecting the two drainage basins. Concealed entrances, guarded by protective runes, open to the east and west. 

The eastern entrance can be found on the bend of the river emptying into the lake Varn Wyraz, with an outlet river that flows to Draksfjord and the Dwarf seaport of _Ungruvalk_ lies in the Sjoktraken. The western gate of forest west of Kraka Ravnsvake on the southern fork of Upper Dypvann. There is a subterranean riverport, Khazid Vulkhrund, that provides a secondary line of defence for the western gate. 

The Draksfjord route allows the Norse Dwarf fleet access to the Frozen Sea as well as the north-flowing rivers leading to other Norse Dwarfholds. It’s also useful for raids against the hated Aeslings. The Dypvann route extends the fleet’s reach to the Sea of Claws where it can protect its mercantile interests, as well as conduct raids on Norscan tribes. 

## **Protective Runestones**
Over the millennia, Norse Dwarfs have both erected and buried large runestones (of sandstone or granite) inscribed with runes that ward against corruption throughout their lands. These runestones act much like Elven Waystones and draw the power of Chaos from the Norse Dwarf lands towards Ulthuan and the Great Vortex. The runestones allow the surrounding region a degree of normality, though they cannot repulse a determined Chaos incursion. 

## **The Giantshome Range**
The Giantshome _(Grontklug)_ Mountains cover eastern Norsca and contain three of the four Norse Dwarfholds (Krakas Ravnsvake, Drak, and Dorden). A fourth hold, Kraka Ornsmotek, lies outside the mountain range. 

These mountains have rich deposits of iron, precious metals (chiefly silver), and gems. The region’s coniferous forests are rich in game. The forest valleys yield quantities of amber. Fish teem in the rivers and coastal waters. The Giantshomes are also noted for large populations of Giants and Trolls, and in turn this attracts Slayers seeking honour and glory in death. 

## **Seafaring**
Norse Dwarfs did not take to the sea as early as those in Barak Varr. Once they decided to contact the southern lands, Norse Dwarfs captured Norscan longships to understand their construction and create their own fleet. Kraka Ravnsvake knew of a subterranean feeder river to the Dypvann and began to construct a hidden harbour for the ships being built. Norse seafarers provided the Dwarfs with knowledge of the sea, but they also needed experience. Norse Dwarfs of Kraka Ravnsvake and Sjoktraken would spend centuries mastering sailing on rivers and coastal waters before venturing across the seas. 

## **Norse Dwarfs**
In –4420 IC Morgrim Grimnirsson returned to Karaz Ankor (the Everlasting Realm, as Dwarfs call the empire ruled by their High King). This was during the Coming of Chaos, and the fate of the Norse Dwarfs would be unknown to their southern kin for millennia. The forces of Chaos effectively isolated Norse Dwarfs for centuries as their holds were surrounded and assumed lost. 

The Norse Dwarfs suffered greatly during this time, but they were also spared the destruction of the War of Vengeance with the Elves and the Goblin Wars which followed. Instead, they battled against warlike Norscan tribes, Chaos beasts, and the Skaven of Clan Moulder. 

In time, Norse Dwarfs began trading with the more outgoing Norscan tribes, such as the Roppsmenn and Bjornlings, teaching them how to brew beer and ferment honey into mead. Relations with the Human Norse have always been strained. Norse Dwarfs are generally thought easygoing by Dwarf standards, but they still record their grievances and seek recompense for them. Over the years the depredations of the Human Norse (called ‘Dumumgi’ by the Dwarfs) have filled chapters of the Books of Grudges held by the Krakas, just as the settling of these grudges has incited further violence from the tribes of the Norse. 

Norse Dwarfs spied on Norscans, even as they fortified their holds, and destroyed trading routes leading to the enemy’s settlements. The Norscans kept their predatory gaze towards the soft southern lands. Norse Dwarfs learned of the world beyond from runaways or captives. 

The knowledge of non–Chaos worshipping Humans gave Norse Dwarfs hope for potential allies as well as trading partners. Moreover, establishing relationships with people from the south could bring information of the Norse Dwarfs’ lost brethren. 

Norse Dwarfs do not tolerate the overt worship of Chaos but overlook the more closeted reverence practised by the less bloodthirsty Norse tribes. Presently the Norse Dwarfs are in a state of low-intensity protracted war with the Baersonlings, Sarl, Graelings, Skaelings, Vargs, and Aeslings, but they do abide by several (albeit strained) treaties of trade and non-hostility with the Bjornlings. 

## Norse Dwarf Characters
A player may like to create a Norse Dwarf Character from one of the Krakas. If so, these rules can be used rather than the rules for Dwarfs on page 36 of the **WFRP Core Rulebook** . 

## **Dwarfs (Norse)**
**Skills:** Climb, Consume Alcohol, Cool, Endurance, Entertain (Storytelling), Evaluate, Language (Khazalid), Language (Norse), Lore (Dwarfs), Melee (Basic), Sail, Trade (Any) 

**Talents:** Carouser _or_ Strong Minded, Magic Resistance, Night Vision, Read/Write _or_ Relentless, Sturdy 

## **Trade and War**
The major impetuses for Norse Dwarf seafaring are trade and war. Though they have been engaged more in the latter than the former through much of their isolation, Norse Dwarfs were able to open trading routes to Erengrad within decades of taking to the sea. 

In time, Norse Dwarfs established trading routes to Marienburg, L’Anguille, and a scattering of smaller Imperial ports on the Sea of Claws, such as Norden. Norse Dwarfs also learned of Karaz Ankor from their time in Erengrad and opened an overland trade route to Karak Vlag, then the northernmost Karaz Ankor Dwarfhold. The partially underground road to Karak Vlag allowed gunpowder weapon technology to make its way into the Norse Dwarfholds. 

Although no longer isolated, Norse Dwarfs remained surrounded by their enemies. Warships allowed Norse Dwarfs to expand the theatre of war, particularly against the Norscan tribes whose raids on Dwarf lands continued. Moreover, Norse Dwarfs could engage in warfare on the open sea and sink many Norscan raiding ships before their enemies could reach their destinations.  Smaller warships traversed Varn Wyraz to keep a lookout for Skaven. 

## **Mountaineering**
Norse Dwarfs reside in mountainous terrain that is covered in snow or ice for much of the year. The many Norse Dwarfs living off the land are experts at moving through the mountains on skis, scaling sheer cliff surfaces, and clambering up the steep mountain slopes. 

## **Relations with Karaz Ankor**
The Norse Dwarfs established relations with Karaz Ankor through their trade with Karak Vlag. In due course, a message came from the High King declaring the longlost Norse Dwarfs owed him fealty as they did the High King before the Coming of Chaos. The Norse Dwarf kings answered that the last High King they owed fealty was Grungni himself, and their fealty remained with the Ancestor God. The High King raged at the response but could not deny its logic nor his northern kin. 

Human observers may find little to distinguish Norse Dwarfs from their southern kin, but due to their history and isolation there are subtle differences in culture and temperament. Norse Dwarfs are more proudly independent than even the Karaz Ankor Dwarfs. They are said to be slower to anger (though not much slower) than other Dwarfs, and somewhat more likely (though only barely) to regard a debt as settled. 

Norse Dwarfs are also notorious for their wild drinking binges, to the extent that even other Dwarfs regard them as _‘a mite too unruly with the ale at times’_ . The Dwarf drinking celebrations of First Quaff (33rd of Plugzeit), Second Breach (33rd of Brauzeit), and Keg End (33rd of Vorhexen) are even more pronounced for their drunken revelry than they are in Karaz Ankor. The celebration of Saga (33rd of Vorgeheim) also has a distinct character, as the Norse Dwarfs solemnly recount their many sufferings at the hands of the followers of Chaos at this time. 

## **Kraka Ravnsvake**
Kraka Ravnsvake is known for its extensive deposits of _okrinaduraz_ , a hard, bluish-grey stone used by artisans to carve the likeness of their revered ancestors and fashion precious jewellery. The mines beneath the Dwarfhold also produce copper, iron, silver, amber, haematite, and a variety of quartz gemstones. 

Kraka Ravnsvake was the first of the Norse Dwarfholds to see the value of reaching the sea. The hold’s king directed engineers and miners to use the underground streams and caverns to create a harbour beneath the stronghold and construct a series of subterranean canals leading to River Dypvann. Later, the engineers built additional canals and diverted underground rivers in the opposite direction to complete _Ungruvalk_ , thereby allowing Kraka Ravnsvake access to Draksfjord. 

## **Government**
Kraka Ravnsvake is currently ruled by King Haarkon Vikramsson and Queen Inga Ottarsdottir of the Ziflinskaud clan, both of whom ascended the throne in 2442 IC. As with other Norse Dwarfholds, the king and queen do not consider themselves subservient to the High King of Karaz Ankor, particularly considering the disappearance of Karak Vlag during the opening stages of the Great War Against Chaos. Faraway Karak Kadrin is now the closest Karaz Ankor Dwarfhold to Norsca. 

King Haarkon and Queen Inga are advised by a council of elders. The continual threat of the Aeslings, Sarl, Skaelings, and Clan Moulder have solidified the council’s support behind an aggressive posture of raids against their enemies and protection of the merchant fleet. 

The king’s treasurer, Asborn Eivinsson, manages to keep the hold’s finances in order, but expresses concern that a massive Aesling assault could imperil Kraka Ravnsvake. In contrast, War Minister Magnek Reidansson argues that the Aeslings are less of a concern as they, too, lost many warriors during the fall of Kraka Drak, and that constant raids have reduced that tribe’s ability to replace their losses. 

## **Fleetmaster**
King Haarkon’s council includes the office of fleetmaster, currently filled by Captain Steinam Kareksson. The fleetmaster is responsible for the condition of the Norse Dwarf navy and its deployment. In addition, the fleetmaster is tasked with gathering information about the maritime activities of the Aeslings, other Norscan tribes living on the Sea of Claws, and the great ports along the sea’s southern coast. The fleetmaster reports information he gathers and recommends a course of action to the king’s council so they can debate and reach an agreement. 

## **Ravnshafnaz**
Ravnshafnaz (‘Raven’s Harbour’) lies in one of the Underdeep levels beneath Kraka Ravnsvake. The harbour contains the oldest shipyard, supporting craftsmen and a fair number of taverns. Many clear quartz gems inscribed with Runes of Light illuminate the cavern. 

Outsiders travelling on the Dypvann are granted access to Ravnshafnaz if they receive a passport etched onto metal foil at the riverport of Khazid Vulkhrund. Norse Dwarfs tolerate Elves better than their southern kin. They see the Asur as people with whom they can trade, but still find their extended company burdensome. Entrances to the Dwarfhold proper and _Ungruvalk_ are heavily guarded and only Norse Dwarfs may pass through. 

## **Hardrak Shipyard**
As old as the Norse Dwarf navy, Hardrak Shipyard is currently run by Shipmaster Berita Frodensdottir, a hardnosed member of the Dwarf Engineers Guild. Berita’s two sons, Marek and Einam Odvarsson, are positioned to take over the shipyard when Berita decides to hang up her tools. Hardrak is no longer as busy as the shipyards at Khazid Vulkhrund or Kazad Ungorhafnaz where normal repair work is handled. Instead, Hardrak Shipyard is where new prototypes of ships or armaments are being designed and tested. Berita works closely on such projects with the fleetmaster. 

## Nautilis
In the past week, engineers at Hardrak Shipyard began design work on a submersible based on those in Barak Varr’s fleet. The plans recently went missing and an internal search has not found them. Shipmaster Berita is looking for discreet individuals to investigate whether an outside spy managed to infiltrate the shipyard or if it was an inside job. In either event, it is of utmost importance that the plans are recovered and the culprit pays for their crime. 

The Hardrak Shipyard has designed a ship that has multiple batteries of cannon which would fire six-pound round balls, and they want to test-fire it while the ship is afloat on River Dypvann. Shipmaster Berita hires the (expendable) Characters to set up targets on the north bank about halfway downriver. There is a possibility that the Characters’ actions could attract the attention of the Troll King’s minions. This, in turn, will provide mobile targets for the live fire. 

## **Berserker Rest Inn**
Owned by the Wyrkarak brewing clan for over a millennium, the two-storeyed, stone-built Berserker Rest Inn is a gathering place for visitors to and inhabitants of Ravnshafnaz. Its large taproom is a popular place for Norse Berserkers to tell stories of their grand deeds and overcoming of incredible odds against them. The innkeeper, Rorek Terjeksson, is a former Berserker who was ‘civilised’ by his wife, Gunva Einarsdottir. Their son, Steinak, and daughter, Janni, assist the couple in brewing the inn’s most popular dark-coloured bitter (‘Grimnir’s Harvest’) and pale lager (‘Valaya’s Tears’). The food at the inn is hearty, but rather spicy for non-Dwarfs. 

## The Berserker’s Tale
An all-too-drunk visitor to Ravnshafnaz openly questions one of the stories a Berserker, Bjarn Morteksson, is telling of his deeds. The visitor claims to have participated in the battle Bjarn is describing and that the Berserker’s tale is not as accurate as he relates. Normally, it is not healthy for one to question a Berserker of his self-described deeds, particularly if said Berserker has been drinking. Fearing the worst outcome for the taproom, Gunva begs the Characters to immediately remove the visitor before a brawl breaks out and furniture starts flying. 

## Slain Elf
A High Elf visitor from Lothern in Ulthuan is found dead in one of the private rooms at the inn. Rorek is concerned the killer may be one of the people whom the haughty Elf insulted in the taproom the night before, but there are no signs of violence on the body other than two puncture wounds near the base of the spine. Rorek asks the Characters to conduct a discrete investigation to identify the murderer before an official inquiry closes down the inn for a time. To make matters worse, the dead Elf is not what he seems. 

## Norse Dwarf Berserkers
Norse Dwarf Berserkers look much like Karaz Ankor Slayers, as both share a reverence for the Ancestor God, Grimnir. Where the two differ greatly is their approach to battle. In contrast to Slayers, Norse Dwarf Berserkers revel in unyielding battle, seeing it as a glory unto itself and a means to honour Grimnir. Those Berserkers who fall in battle are accorded funerals that honour the fallen as great heroes, while those who survive tell stories of valorous deeds. 

## **Kraka Ravnsvake Navy**
Kraka Ravnsvake was the first to advocate for the establishment of maritime trade and a fleet to protect it. No such tradition previously existed among the Norse Dwarfholds. All that was needed were ships, some safe ports, and an outlet to the sea. 

## **Norse Dwarf Warships**
With no tradition of seafaring to build upon, the first Norse Dwarf warships looked very much like Norscan longships. The design, portage, and shallow draft of these longships made them ideal for travel on rivers such as the Dypvann and the Susna (connecting Varn Wyraz to Draksfjord) as well as coastal waters. Norse Dwarfs retained this design for many centuries. 

The first changes to Norse Dwarf warships resulted from encounters with Norscans. Chaos marauders would lash their ships together before battle to form fighting platforms. As a result of those encounters, Norse Dwarfs equipped the bow of their ships with bolt throwers to hole the enemy’s hull below the water line, sinking them at a safe distance. Bolt heads were designed to penetrate timber and make extraction difficult. 

## **Grubark Gearing System**
**Cost:** 400 GC for Little to Average ships; may not be applied to larger ships. **Weight:** 120 Encumbrance points. 

This vessel uses an ingenious yet simple gearing system to allow a handful of Dwarfs to operate a bank of sweeps. The minimum number of crew needed to row the boat is reduced to a quarter of its original number (rounding up any fractions). Rowers also benefit from +1 SL to Endurance Tests made to see if they become exhausted after a shift at the oars (see page 105). 

The gearing system is a complex and intricate piece of machinery. If the Oars Location takes a Critical Hit, roll d10. On a 5 or more the gearing system is ruined in addition to the effects of the Critical Hit. 

**Example:** A Longship has an Oars score of 6 (30), meaning that a crew of 30 rowers can move the vessel at M6. If the Longship was equipped with a Grubark Gearing System its Oars score would be 6 (8). 

The exchange of ideas with Karak Vlag engineers brought new innovations. Gunwales were reinforced with steel, and ships broadened to keep drafts as shallow as possible. Swivel guns or small cannons (called ‘ _dalkrit_ ’ in Khazalid) were mounted on a raised bow or stern to fire grapeshot or (in the case of the cannon) four-pound round shot. 

The requirement that Norse Dwarf ships needed to travel to their ports on rivers, however, meant that technology could only take them so far. Concurrently, Norse Dwarf engineers devised a simple gearing system that allowed a handful of Dwarfs to operate a bank of oars (much like the early ‘grubark’ craft of Barak Varr). Norse Dwarf mariners were, as a result, fresher when combat was inevitable. 

Whilst it is now considered archaic by the Dwarfs of Karaz Ankor, the grubark design of vessel remains popular amongst the Norse Dwarfs.

## **Growth of Norse Dwarf Navy**
The growth of the Norse Dwarf navy was the primary concern of Kraka Ravnsvake shipmasters, as an escort-less merchant fleet would be susceptible to Norscan attacks. In time, Kraka Drak followed suit with its own navy, primarily to raid Aesling villages and protect whaling fleets in the Frozen Sea. Once captains and crews gained experience on the rivers and coastal waters, there were no shortages of warriors who wanted to take the fight to the Norscans. By the time of the Great War Against Chaos, there were roughly 250 warships in the Norse Dwarf navy. 

## **Kazad Ungorhafnaz**
With the completion of _Ungruvalk_ , the fortress of Kazad Ungorhafnaz was built to guard the concealed eastern entrance. The entrance is protected by Runes of Enemy Detection within the interior of the gate: one set to detect the presence of Skaven (emitting a greenish glow) and the other Humans (reddish). When a Norse Dwarf ship arrives on the Upper Susna from Varn Wyraz, a sentry from the watchtower above the gate blows a large horn directly down a shaft to the fortress below, notifying the gatekeepers to open the entrance. The importance of Kazad Ungorhafnaz became clear with the fall of Kraka Drak to the forces of Valmir Aesling. 

## **Securing Sjoktraken**
The War in the Mountains forced Kraka Ravnsvake to secure the port town of Sjoktraken against the Aesling invaders. Many Ravnsvake gunships sailed through Ungruvalk to Draksfjord, joining the local naval vessels which had cast off onto the water with guns ready. Lucky for the Norse Dwarf navy, the Aeslings were solely focused on destroying Kraka Drak to the exclusion of anything else. The Ravnsvake fleetmaster took command of the Sjoktraken fleet. 

## **Current Deployment**
There are currently 75 warships in the Sjoktraken fleet, mostly coastal and river gunships tasked with protecting the trade routes with Krakas Dorden and Ornsmotek. Raids of revenge on the nearby Aesling villages are part of their mission. The Ravnsvake fleet has 190 warships to protect the hold and its trading routes, as well as to raid Norscans: 15 on Varn Wyraz, 35 refitting in port, and 140 on the Sea of Claws. 

## The Ancestors at Sea
Dwarfs do not venerate Manann, seeing him as a Human deity (‘with Elven roots, no less!’ — so the Loremasters are known to carp). Instead, they look to their own venerated ancestors for inspiration and protection, just as they do on land. 

Grungni, the ancestor associated with mining and craftsmanship, is rarely beseeched at sea. It is an alien environment, for he is seen as a delver of the mountainsides rather than a traveller upon the waves. Many Dwarf vessels bear icons of Grungni, though these are not placed upon a vessel to attract his beneficence, but rather as a mark that the shipwright who built the craft did so to the standards Grungni himself would approve of. 

Grimnir, the ancestor associated with warfare and vengeance, is often called upon by Dwarfs at sea. Combat upon the ocean is even more desperate than it is on land, for there is nowhere for a disadvantaged side to reposition, or a losing side to retreat to. Grimnir’s cult of doom seeking and death dealing therefore appeals to many Dwarf mariners even if they stop short of taking the Slayer Oath. Those who have taken up the path of the Slayer often consider taking up a life at sea, though they make for rather perverse shipmates, desiring to meet with the same monsters and reavers that most sailors hope to avoid. In some cases, such as that of the infamous Long Drong, Dwarf crews are made entirely of those who seek a Slayer’s destiny. 

Valaya is the Dwarf ancestor associated with hearth, home, and healing. Whilst she might be commonly imagined at the roaring hearth of a Dwarf King’s greatest hall, she is popular with Dwarf mariners, and often beseeched by those who sail the oceans. She is seen as a protecting ancestor, and the one most likely to ensure that a Dwarf crew make it back to port safely. Valaya is also the ancestor associated with brewing and the inventor of runic script, so she is vaunted by Dwarf sailors whenever they consult their _Book of Charts_ , or warm themselves with a tankard of grog. 

A ship that is captained by a Dwarf, and that has a sizable contingent of Dwarfs amongst the crew, does not suffer or benefit from Manann’s Mood (see page 130) provided that the GM is satisfied that they are not intentionally trying to insult Manann. 

## **Skaldor ‘Reaver’ Lotharksson** _Norse Dwarf Sea Captain_
## **Motivation:** Vengeance **.**
**Short-Term Ambition:** Exact revenge on the Aeslings for the fall of Kraka Drak. 

**Long-Term Ambition:** Secure long-term safety of Norse Dwarf realms. 

Skaldor’s clan was one of the first which took to the sea when the first Norse Dwarf ship launched in 1070 IC. Like many of the _Varrundi_ clan, Skaldor took to the sea as a beardling (the Reikspiel equivalent of _Knublstubi_ , a Kazalid term for a callow Dwarf youth) and worked his way up the ranks. He learned how to escort Norse Dwarf merchant vessels, and also led raids against the Sarls and the Skaelings. 

Skaldor’s outlook was shaped by the War in the Mountains in which the Aesling High King, Valmir, fought an 88-year campaign to bring down Kraka Drak. Even though the fallen Dwarfhold is being reclaimed and reoccupied over a century after its destruction, the hatred of Norscans among many Norse Dwarfs has only grown since that time. 

In 2485 IC, Skaldor received a promotion to captain of his own warship, _‘Hammer of Chaos’ (Grund A Dum)_ . A dalkrit mounted on the bow and swivel gun on the _Hammer of_ stern serve as the ship’s main weapons. The _Chaos_ carries 80 rowers/warriors, each equipped with bow, hand weapons, shield, and mail. As a captain of the Kraka Ravnsvake navy, Skaldor pledged to live by three standing orders: protect Norse Dwarf merchant ships, gather information on the disposition of enemy vessels or warbands, and conduct raids against the enemies of Norse Dwarfs. 

It was the relish with which Skaldor proceeded on the third order that gave him his nickname of ‘Reaver’. His crew includes a fair number of Berserkers looking for any opportunity to slay Norscans and revel in battle. Life with Skaldor could be short, but it is always exciting. 

## **Skaldor as Patron**
In his capacity of gathering information on the enemies of Norse Dwarfs, Skaldor is not beyond utilising nonDwarfs to assist him. Characters can come to Skaldor’s attention whenever he is in one of the Old World ports. Perhaps some deed catches his eye in a taproom or on the streets. If the Characters have demonstrated an ability to discreetly gather information or shadow someone, Skaldor may give them an opportunity to prove their worth. Satisfactorily completing a small task may lead to better paying, and more dangerous, jobs. 

## **Prestige Adventure: Stalking Chaos Marauders**
Recently, a Norse Dwarf warship and several merchant ships were waylaid north of the Bay of Blades. Skaldor accepted the assignment to ‘bring Grimnir’s wrath upon those responsible for the attack’. His first task is to determine whether the culprits are Sarls or Skaelings. 

Skaldor needs a trusted group of tough and discreet non-Dwarfs who are skilled in the wilderness to follow the trail from the wreckage, penetrate inland, locate the perpetrators, and report back. Skaldor is not interested in the slaughter of Norse villagers, but killing their marauders is always considered worthy of reward. 

Skaldor expects the group to take revenge on the perpetrators if they can or, if not, report back so he and his Dwarfs can do so.

## **Rune of Speed**
The Rune of Speed inscribed on a hand weapon provides the wielder with a +10 modifier to their Initiative when attacking with the weapon. 

## **Rune of Striking**
The Rune of Striking inscribed on a hand weapon provides the wielder with a +10 modifier to their Weapon Skill when attacking with the weapon. 

## **Rune of Clear Seeing**
The Rune of Clear Seeing inscribed on a lens allows a user to see through fog and mist. Perception Tests made by someone using the lens are not affected by the rules for Visibility (see page 106). The Rune of Clear Seeing cannot see through magicallyinduced mists (such as created by _Illusion or Mystifying Miasma_ spells) but reveals these as magical by tinting them greenish. 

## **Rune of Farseeing**
The Rune of Farseeing allows the user to peer through the inscribed lens and see objects up to one mile away as if they were much closer, like a telescope. This requires an uninterrupted line of sight to the object
